name: module-size
question: Which ULADP modules (directories bearing a README.md) exceed the soft token band (default ~4000, M2) by byte-based estimate, and which directories look like undocumented modules (>=3 code files, no README)?
cost_provenance: measured 2026-07-07 on the ULDF framework repo (1276 tracked files) under Git Bash (win32; slowest supported environment) -- ~1.0s via the git ls-tree fast path; declared pessimistically at the fast-lane ceiling per ORACLE-COST-01

schema.over_band: array of {path, est_tokens, band} -- modules over the soft band (advisory), sorted by est_tokens desc, capped
schema.no_readme: array of {path, est_tokens, code_files} -- dirs with >=3 code files and no README.md (possible undocumented modules)
schema.no_data: array of {path, reason} -- paths that could not be analyzed (unreadable); never a silent pass
schema.enum_mode: one of: git (ls-tree fast path), find (filesystem fallback), none (no-data)
schema.briefing: string (empty when status=pass; one-liner suitable for a warn surface)

fallback: Estimate per-directory tokens by hand: for each directory bearing a README.md, sum the byte sizes of the files directly in it and divide by 4 (the segments/-uladp/compliance_architecture.md convention); a result over ~4000 is an over-band module worth decomposing. Or run /0-uldf-uladp-compliance --architecture for the full sizing + boundary analysis. git ls-tree -r -l HEAD gives per-file sizes in one command.

provenance.note: Scrutiny ADD A6 / finding P0-7: the framework's own Enforcement Placement Principle (detection that is pure arithmetic belongs in code, not prose) + Oraculurgy Part 11 jointly mandate a deterministic module-sizing oracle, yet trajectory-cap shipped a deterministic size-cap oracle for ONE markdown file while the doctrinal per-module token cap had none. This is that oracle. M2 re-derivation: the ~4k number is restated as a SOFT BAND (a tripwire proxy for one session's reliable comprehension per Principle 2.9's capacity formula + Team-Topologies cognitive-load framing / CTD-16 horizon), NOT a context-window-fit claim (obsolete at 1M contexts). ADVISORY by design (status=warn, exit 0): a hard cap invites split-for-the-metric micro-modules (perverse incentive) -- report, do not refuse. The 500-token summary-compressibility test (Principle 2.9) is the better companion diagnostic but is agentic, not this oracle's job; this oracle is the deterministic tripwire.

config.comment: Soft band (advisory tripwire), overridable per-project via .claude/config.json moduleSize.softBandTokens. Token estimate = sum(direct-file bytes)/4. The band is a proxy for one-session comprehension, NOT a context-window-fit cliff (M2). Keep the git ls-tree fast path for the <2s Part 11 fast-lane contract.
